The full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`). 

## Summary

The spec: `membershipTier` becomes `'GOLD'` when the owner's household (owners sharing the same `householdId`) has 3+ members after the create; otherwise the existing BRONZE/SILVER rules apply.

I implemented this with minimal structural impact — three files, all small and cohesive:

1. **`HouseholdTier.java`** (new) — a tiny stateless helper mirroring the existing `BulkSignup`/`MembershipTier` style. `isGold(owner, repo)` counts how many owners share the owner's `householdId` (reusing the existing `HouseholdId.of`) and returns true at ≥3.

2. **`RespondWithOwner.java`** (GET) & **`RespondWithOwnerCreated.java`** (POST) — each got a 3-line guard that overrides the mapper-derived tier with `"GOLD"` when the household qualifies. Both already had `OwnerRepository` injected, so no new dependencies.

### Why this shape
The tier was previously derived in the big `OwnerMapper`/`Owner` machinery. Adding the GOLD rule there would have meant a new field + getter/setter on the large `Owner` entity and changing `MembershipTier.of`'s signature — each edit paying the full `WMC_other` of a large class, multiplied across ~5 files. Instead I added the behaviour as a self-contained unit and touched only the two small responder classes (each with WMC_other ≈ 0), keeping every changed function at CC ≤ 2 and the file count at 3. The BRONZE/SILVER path is completely untouched — GOLD simply takes precedence when it applies.
